submission.justification: Selection-S2 has the highest nominal expected significance (4.1 sigma in the 2025 summary at 50% efficiency), but its validation-region data/MC yield disagreement is 35%, well above the 10% tolerance agreed with the conveners. Its jet-substructure inputs are poorly modelled, so its background estimate is not robust and it is excluded. Among the remaining strategies, Selection-S1 (neural network, kinematic variables) has the highest expected significance (3.4 sigma) and passes the validation check at 6% disagreement, versus 3% for the cut-based Selection-S3 (2.6 sigma). I recommend Selection-S1 at a 50% signal-efficiency working point, the reference point used in the 2025 sensitivity study and inside the 20-80% constraint. Caveats: the 2025 significances are statistical-only and I had no tool that returns a current efficiency scan, so the 50% working point was not re-optimised and the significance figures may be stale. The 6% disagreement is within tolerance but not negligible, so it should be included as a systematic uncertainty on the background.
